blocks.text: 8. Strength
The Taming of the Beast
Numbered eight, a woman stands calmly before a lion, gently closing its jaws with her hands.
While The Chariot represented the conquest of enemies through force and armor, Strength represents the conquest of the self through love and patience.
She is the archetype of Fortitude—not the physical power to destroy, but the spiritual power to endure.
She teaches that the wildest beasts are not tamed by chains, but by the confident touch of compassion.
The Infinite Spirit
Above her head floats the lemniscate, the symbol of infinity, which also appeared above the Magician.
This connects her to the divine source of energy.
It suggests that her strength is inexhaustible because it does not rely on muscle, but on spirit.
The lion represents our primal nature—our rage, lust, and raw passion.
She does not kill the lion, nor does she fear it; she honors it and integrates it, understanding that this animal energy is the fuel for her spiritual survival.
The Principle of Resilience
Strength embodies the principle of resilience and sublimation.
It is the ability to face suffering or difficulty without breaking.
Unlike the Chariot’s brittle armor which can be pierced, her strength is fluid and flexible.
She demonstrates that true power is quiet.
It is the courage to remain open and vulnerable in the face of danger, trusting in the supremacy of the higher self over the lower instincts.
The Agency of Persuasion
The agency of this card is persuasion rather than coercion.
It represents the "soft power" that influences outcomes through character and presence.
It asks us to approach problems not with aggression, but with understanding.
It suggests that the most effective way to control a situation is to first control one's own reaction to it.
She holds the lion’s mouth not to silence it, but to guide its roar.
An Invitation to Softness
Drawing Strength is a call to tame the beasts within you with kindness.
It asks you to forgive your own imperfections and to have patience with your own anger.
It invites you to approach conflict with a gentle hand, reminding you that a soft answer turns away wrath.
It is an assurance that you already possess the inner resources to weather any storm.
